input.quote: 4.3 Ownership of the Wet Segment shall be as shown in Schedule B to this Agreement. The Wet Segment of APCN 2 shall be owned by the Parties in common and undivided shares.
input.rationale: Full-text searches for "intellectual property", "proprietary", "licence/license", "patent/copyright/know-how/invention", "work product/deliverable" and "data" return no IP, deliverables or Customer Data provisions anywhere in this APCN 2 Construction & Maintenance Agreement, and the candidate clauses are asset/capacity ownership rather than IP: 4.1/4.3 (p0107, p0119) allocate Segment ownership per Schedule B, 12.2 (p0187) gives us Allocated Capacity on an ownership basis, and the IRU definition (p0054) expressly conveys no ownership. The rule's direction risk therefore does not arise: there is no Vendor supplying deliverables or work product, nothing assigns any Teleglobe IP or data to the other Parties, and no counterparty licence over our data exists. The co-ownership of the Wet Segment "in common and undivided shares" is physical plant co-ownership inherent to a consortium cable, and it is paired with our own capacity on an ownership basis plus an unrestricted right to exploit it ("any Party is entitled to make available any of its Allocated Capacity for use by other Carriers on any commercial basis without any restrictions", 12.22), so it is not the joint IP ownership without exploitation rights that the walk-away targets. Confidentiality (31.1) additionally protects data we supply, with a five-year tail. Minor point noted rather than redlined: the Agreement contains no residual IP/Customer Data ownership statement; we see no need to import vendor-style deliverable assignment or data-processing licence language into a co-ownership consortium instrument, and we would add it only if a deliverables or data-processing arrangement is later layered on. No redline proposed; the position is acceptable as drafted and flagging it would risk diluting our existing ownership rights.
